messages:
Alex W: Hey team — need to run a short-lived SIEM export for a third-party vuln triage vendor. They need 14 days of auth/authz logs. Question: can we do an export with scoped rows + redaction, ephemeral KMS unwrap, and a JIT RBAC lease instead of changing roles permanently?
Maria T: Short answer: yes, but we need ticketed justification + JIT lease + export-level scrub. Policy: https://redwood/internal/security/log-export-policy (see section 'ephemeral-consumer'). :+1:
Sanjeev K: Is 14 days hard requirement? We usually recommend 7d for external vendors unless legal requires more. Longer TTL increases blast radius.
Alex W: Vendor insists 14d for historical correlation with an exploit timeline. Legal is ok with a controlled export.
Elaine R: We should use the kms-proxy flow: create an ephemeral CMK grant (timeboxed), wrap export with envelope encryption, and log the grant in audit events. That avoids unwrap of long-term CMK.
Samir P: Also: do NOT change human RBAC. Create a service-account scoped to the export S3 bucket (read-only), insert principal into OPA allowlist for that TTL, and issue a short-lived token from our STS. No permanent role changes.
Maria T: +1. Approval path: fill this ticket template and tag @security-lead. I can pre-approve once infra confirms ephemeral key grant and scrub rules.
Alex W: Ok adding template here so it's consistent:
```
- request_owner: Alex W
- vendor: SecureTriage Ltd
- data_scope: auth, session, token-audit (no PII fields)
- retention_ttl: 14d
- reasons: vuln correlation for CVE-2025-XXXX triage
- approval: security, legal, infra
```
logbot: New ticket created: SEC-5134 by Alex W — https://redwood/secure/SEC-5134
Sanjeev K: For the export scrub rules, please run the redaction job with this config (example):
```yaml
export:
  redact_fields:
    - user.email
    - user.ip_last_octet
  sample_rate: 100%
  mask_strategy: hash:salt_per_export
```
Elaine R: Infra action items: 1) create ephemeral CMK grant for SEC-5134 for 15d, 2) provision service-account with bucket-only access, 3) enable object-level audit logging to the secure-audit bucket.
Samir P: Ops: can we enforce deny-by-default network egress from the vendor's VM to prevent copying? Maybe we can lock export bucket policy to vendor IP list and pre-signed URL TTL.
Infra (via Maria T): We can do pre-signed URLs + bucket policy allowlist. Pre-signed TTL will be 72h; for >72h we rotate the presign and push objects to the vendor via an ephemeral transfer job we control.
Alex W: Who signs off for RBAC/OPA changes? I want to avoid manual role updates.
Maria T: Security lead or myself. OPA policy change must be PR-reviewed and auto-tested. We'll not change builtin roles — we'll use the ephemeral-service-account pattern.
Samir P: Audit question: will the export action itself be captured in an immutable audit event (who requested, who approved, grant id)? We need that for IR postmortem.
Elaine R: Yes — export orchestration writes a single export descriptor event to our audit stream with grant_id, ticket, scrub rules, and CMK_grant_id. That's non-deletable and retained 1 year.
Alex W: Sounds good. I'll file SEC-5134 with the template and request ephemeral CMK grant for 15d (14d data + 1d buffer). Tagging @Maria T for infra and @Security-Lead for approval.
Maria T: I'll review within 2 business hours once infra confirms the CMK grant pattern. If anything blocks, we'll fallback to scoped 7d export and escalate.
Samir P: One more nit — record the vendor's DPA consent doc in the ticket and attach a hashed copy in audit (not raw pdf).
Alex W: Will do. Thanks all. :pray:
Maria T: Closing notes: no permanent role/role-binding changes, use ephemeral key + service-account, ticket + approval required, audit descriptor generated. I'll update the policy doc with the example snippets.
